headline: Oil spikes on Iran, PSX wobbles then shrugs it off — banks and fertilizer do the heavy lifting while autos and cement eat the volatility.
summary: Brent crude jumped 3.6% in a day to $78.73 after fresh US-Iran strikes, and that oil/geopolitics story is why the desk's risk gauge sits at a 'moderate' 47/100 today. PSX actually held up reasonably well through it: KSE-100 fell 2.48% on the worst day (Jul 9) but clawed back 0.54% by Friday, and foreigners stayed net buyers (Rs2.37bn) through the whole week. The rupee is steady near 278/USD, SBP's reserves just jumped $1.94bn to $18.47bn, and inflation eased to 11.1% — none of that is falling apart even with oil jumpy. Regime reads neutral: the desk is leaning toward quality names in banks, fertilizer and power, and staying wary of cement, autos, steel and OMCs where oil and rupee costs bite hardest into results season.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: SBP is holding its policy rate at 11.5% (next decision Jul 27), which keeps bank margins wide, and the sector's biggest names (UBL, HBL, MCB) are the ones leading July's bounce.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Low-beta, defensive names (FFC beta 0.28, ENGROH beta 0.05) barely move with the market — exactly what the desk wants to lean on while oil-driven headlines whip the index around.

sectors.name: Power
sectors.why: HUBC and peers carry covered dividends above 6% and don't chase the market's swings (beta ~0.47), a ballast sector when Middle East jitters hit sentiment.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Oil at $78.73 (+3.6% in a day) raises fuel and power costs baked into cement production, and the sector was among last week's worst performers (-436 index points WoW).

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: A soft-ish rupee near 278/USD raises the cost of imported parts, and it's notable both of today's active technical triggers (HCAR, GAL) sit in this macro-flagged sector — a real tension worth watching.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: PSO's net margin is a wafer-thin 1.4%; the Jul 11 fuel-price hike (+Rs13.18 petrol, +Rs13.80 diesel) is a pass-through to consumers, not a profit driver, so margins stay squeezed.

sectors.name: Steel
sectors.why: Same story as cement — imported input costs rise with a firmer oil price and softer rupee, squeezing margins right into earnings season.

watchlist.angle: Banks are macro-favoured, and UBL's consolidation-break strategy has a strong record on its own history — 76% hit rate over 38 trades, +2.18% average net gain, and it held up out-of-sample too (80% hit on the last 15). The stock is already trending hard (+21.9% over 20 sessions, closing above both its 20- and 50-day averages) and screens attractive on fundamentals: 8.52x earnings, 30% net margin, a 6.61% dividend yield covered by just 56% of profit. Results are estimated for Jul 22 (scraped, unconfirmed date).
watchlist.risk: RSI is at 67 — a lot of the move may already be priced in, and a soft earnings print could trigger profit-taking fast.

watchlist.angle: FFC ranks #2 on the desk's predictability list (score 67.3) and fertilizer is one of macro's favoured sectors right now. Its best-proven setup, a 52-week-high breakout, has fired 27 times historically with a 78% win rate that held up out-of-sample (71%) — the stock isn't at that trigger level today (RSI 51.7, 3.3% below its 20-day high), so this is a name to watch, not an active signal. Fundamentals lean constructive: forward P/E of 7.02 versus 9.39 trailing signals expected earnings growth, and the 6.58% yield is comfortably covered. Results estimated Jul 29 (scraped, unconfirmed).
watchlist.risk: No live trigger firing today — the setup hasn't confirmed. A miss on the Jul 29 print would undercut the improving-earnings case.

watchlist.angle: Power generation is macro-favoured, and HUBC screens attractive on fundamentals: 6.7x trailing earnings (cheap third of the market), a 64.8% net margin, and a 6.61% yield covered by 58% of profit. Its 52-week-high breakout strategy has a strong track record (64% hit rate historically, 75% out-of-sample), and the stock sits at #8 on the desk's predictability rankings (score 60.5).
watchlist.risk: Not an active trigger today (RSI 50.7, price 3.8% off its 20-day high) — a name to watch rather than a setup in motion, and results aren't due until late August, so there's no near-term catalyst to force the issue.

watchlist.angle: The desk's one high-confidence live trigger firing today: a golden cross (50-day SMA crossing above the 200-day) that has won 60% of the time on HCAR's own 10-trade history and held up out-of-sample. Strategy engine levels: entry 245.56, stop 233.28, target 270.12.
watchlist.risk: Fundamentals flag caution — a thin 2.6% net margin, a small 10-trade backtest sample, and autos is a sector macro is actively steering away from given rupee-driven import costs. A live trigger firing doesn't override a weak fundamental and macro backdrop — worth treating carefully.

watchlist.angle: The second live trigger on the board today: a 50-day high breakout, medium confidence with a 56% historical hit rate over 27 trades. Fundamentals are mixed but improving — cheap at 5.19x trailing earnings with the forward multiple dropping to 4.68, pointing to expected earnings growth.
watchlist.risk: Small-cap (Rs34.7bn market cap) with thinner liquidity, the out-of-sample hit rate on this setup is a coin-flip (50%), and autos remains a sector macro is flagging as a headwind.

catalysts.event: HCAR, NESTLE, FFL results (scraped estimates, unconfirmed)
SBP MPC meeting — first FY27 monetary policy decision

risks: Middle East conflict escalation — Brent is already +3.6% in a day on US-Iran strikes; a further spike widens Pakistan's import bill and could push SBP back toward a hawkish stance.
SBP's Jul 27 MPC decision is a live event risk — inflation at 11.1% is easing but the real policy rate is barely positive, leaving room for a surprise either way.

Global risk appetite is wobbling — VIX jumped 9% in a day (still a low absolute level at 16.4, but the direction matters); a genuine risk-off swing abroad tends to pull foreign flows out of frontier markets like PSX fast.
